ActuatorConfig.mount: where it sits on the 3D model; written only when set

Command.children: nested commands, meaningful ONLY for ``kind in ("if", "while")`` (the compound/control-block kinds) -- empty for every other kind. A plain ``list[Command]``, not a separate type, so the same tree-walking code (validation, reference-scanning, execution) recurses uniformly regardless of nesting depth.
Command.enabled: False leaves the command (and its children) out of the run, as if commented out; it is still validated, so enabling it again cannot break the scenario. Saved only when False (``Scenario.to_dict``), so older files load unchanged.
Command.label: optional user-facing name (e.g. ``"Prop to Periapsis"`` instead of an auto-numbered ``"Propagate3"``) -- purely cosmetic, never referenced by other commands/resources.
Command.params: kind-specific fields -- see :meth:`validate` for exactly what each kind requires/accepts.

OrbitIC.semi_major_axis_km: type == "classical_elements" (angles in degrees, matching the rest of this codebase's convention -- see mission_config.py in ../missionAnalysis). Exactly one of true_anomaly_deg/mean_anomaly_deg is used, chosen by anomaly_type -- mean anomaly is the natural input for a mission design spec (e.g. "M0 at epoch"), true anomaly for a specific geometric snapshot; engine.service converts mean -> true via Kepler's equation before calling elem2rv (which only accepts true anomaly).

PhasingKeepingConfig.control_law: one of PHASING_CONTROL_LAWS: drift_orbit, mean_oe, hill_pd meanOEFeedback outputs a force, so its K is this per-kilogram gain times the follower's mass at the start of the run.

PhasingKeepingConfig.max_drift_days: [day] safety cap on the drift coast phase
PhasingKeepingConfig.mean_oe_gain: [m^2/s^3] "mean_oe": diagonal of K per kg of spacecraft
PhasingKeepingConfig.reconfiguration_interval_days: [day] only matters if target_separation_km has >1 entry
PhasingKeepingConfig.restore_tolerance_fraction: [-] "close enough, stop drifting" threshold, same units
PhasingKeepingConfig.target_separation_km: [km] one or more along-track distances ahead of the chief
PhasingKeepingConfig.tolerance_fraction: [-] trigger threshold, as a fraction of the current target separation

PowerConfig.battery_initial_soc: [-] initial state of charge, fraction of capacity, 0 <= x <= 1

PropellantBudgetConfig.clearance_sma_drop_km: [km] AD10 suggests >= 5 km for formation flyers

PropellantBudgetConfig.controlled_reentry_last_burn_m_s: [m/s] the last burn, before its 15% margin
PropellantBudgetConfig.disposal_lifetime_years: [year] orbit lifetime after the disposal burn
PropellantBudgetConfig.dry_mass_includes_margin: else the system margin below is added (Sec. 5.10)
PropellantBudgetConfig.hall_thruster_ignition_kg: [kg] cathode start-up losses over the mission
PropellantBudgetConfig.isp_s: [s] None = the orbit thruster's (station keeping etc.)
PropellantBudgetConfig.mission_years: [year] nominal operations from the epoch (AD10 Sec. 5.7)
PropellantBudgetConfig.tank_capacity_kg: [kg] maximum propellant load (Sec. 5.8); 0 = the budget's own total
PropellantBudgetConfig.thrust_angle_deg: [deg] thruster axis vs wanted thrust direction (Sec. 5.11)

RFLinkConfig.antenna_beamwidth_deg: [deg] half-power beamwidth of the spacecraft's downlink antenna pattern. None (the default) keeps every existing scenario's exact prior behavior (no pointing-loss term at all -- same as before this field existed). Set together with CommsPointingConfig to make the link margin respond to the spacecraft's own actual achieved antenna pointing error (see engine.link_budget's module docstring for the parabolic-pattern approximation this applies: L_point_dB = 12*(pointing_error_deg / antenna_beamwidth_deg)^2, the standard textbook falloff for a Gaussian/parabolic-reflector main lobe).
RFLinkConfig.antenna_boresight_b: Body-frame boresight of the downlink antenna. None falls back to comms_pointing.antenna_boresight_b; "cosine" and "table" need one of the two, since the gain then depends on the real attitude.
RFLinkConfig.antenna_front_to_back_db: [dB] "cosine" only: gain behind the ground plane, below the peak
RFLinkConfig.antenna_gain_table: [off-boresight angle deg, gain dBi] pairs, angles rising from 0; linear in dB between them, the last gain beyond the last angle.
RFLinkConfig.antenna_mount: Where the antenna sits on the 3D model (its boresight and beamwidth default to the two above); written only when set.
RFLinkConfig.antenna_pattern: How the spacecraft antenna's gain falls off away from boresight, used wherever the downlink is evaluated live (engine.data_handling's link gate: a DataHandlingConfig, or any pattern other than "fixed"): "fixed" -- tx_antenna_gain_dbi in every direction (minus the antenna_beamwidth_deg pointing loss above, if set); "cosine" -- a patch antenna: gain G0*cos^n(theta) in front of the ground plane, n from the peak gain (engine.link_budget. cosine_exponent), antenna_front_to_back_db below the peak behind it; "table" -- antenna_gain_table, read off the antenna's datasheet.
RFLinkConfig.required_ebno_db: [dB] required Eb/N0 for the assumed modulation/coding

RoeFormationConfig.continuous_gain: [m^2/s^3] "continuous": diagonal of K per kg (as phasing_keeping.mean_oe_gain); ten times phasing's default, which leaves metre-scale ROE errors growing
RoeFormationConfig.correction_window_days: [day] "impulsive": time to bring the mean longitude back by drifting
RoeFormationConfig.differential_drag: "impulsive": estimate the steady decay of the relative semi-major axis that differential drag causes (from the measured mean ROE) and plan the hold around it, once it is large enough to matter
RoeFormationConfig.drag_estimate_window_days: [day] "impulsive": how far back the decay is fitted
RoeFormationConfig.max_burn_fraction_of_orbit: [-] "impulsive": a burn longer than this fraction of an orbit is split over several orbits, so it stays close to an impulse
RoeFormationConfig.target_refresh_s: [s] "continuous": how often the element target follows the chief's J2 drift
RoeFormationConfig.tolerance_m: [m] "impulsive": how far each part of the mean ROE may stray before a correction: a*|d(da)|, a*|d(dlambda)|, a*|d(de)|, a*|d(di)|

RoeTargetConfig.roe_m: [m] a*(da, dlambda, dex, dey, dix, diy): relative semi-major axis, mean longitude, eccentricity vector, inclination vector

Scenario.config_file: The project configuration file this scenario uses (transparency audit, Phase 3b; spacemissionstudio.config.files): YAML naming parameters and the values the project gives them. Absolute, or relative to the scenario file's folder; None: every parameter has its default.
Scenario.configuration: That file, read (config.registry.Configuration): set where the scenario is loaded (load_scenario, the GUI's editor), never saved, left out of the scenario's hash and of comparisons; the run's provenance records the file's SHA-256 and each value it changes.
Scenario.epoch_utc: ISO 8601, e.g. "2030-01-01T00:00:00" -- single source of truth for time; TAI/TT/ET are DERIVED (see engine/time_system.py), never separately stored, so they cannot drift out of sync with epoch_utc.
Scenario.fsw_exports: list[FswExportRecord], at most one per spacecraft
Scenario.simulation_mode: Chosen up front (the GUI's scenario editor puts it at the top of the form, "before starting with anything else" per the feature request this responds to): "full_attitude" (the default, and everything this schema always supported) simulates attitude/sensors/actuators/FSW/ power normally. "orbit_only" is a beginner-friendly, deliberately STRICTER mode for pure orbit-propagation questions (delta-V budgets, orbit lifetime, station-keeping cadence, ...) where attitude doesn't matter and modeling it is only friction: no spacecraft may set fsw_mode/sensors/actuators/power in this mode (Scenario.validate() rejects it with a specific error naming the offending spacecraft and field, same "don't let something look configured that isn't" honesty as everywhere else in this schema) -- the spacecraft is simulated as a cannonball with SpacecraftConfig.drag_area_m2/srp_area_m2 as its average cross-section. station_keeping/phasing_keeping/ constant_thrust remain available in EITHER mode: none of them need attitude knowledge (their thrust directions are prograde or orbit-frame-relative, not a commanded body axis).

SensorConfig.mount: where it sits on the 3D model; written only when set

SimSettings.record_interval_s: [s] How often results are recorded; 0 = every dynamics step. Long runs need this: a 5-year run at a 30 s step is ~5 million samples per series. Controller burn flags record "fired since the last sample", so short burns still show; positions, angles and access flags are snapshots, so anything shorter than this (e.g. a ground-station pass) can fall between two samples.
SimSettings.seed: The run's random seed. Every model with a random generator (sensor noise, navigation error, faults) gets its own seed derived from this one and its name (engine.seeds.assign_rng_seeds), so two sensors never draw the same noise, and the same scenario gives the same run. Change it for another realisation of the noise.

SolarArrayConfig.deploy_direction_b: body-frame direction from the hinge to the tip
SolarArrayConfig.first_mode_hz: [Hz] first bending frequency, hub held fixed
SolarArrayConfig.initial_deflection_deg: [deg] about the hinge, positive toward normal_b
SolarArrayConfig.normal_b: body-frame normal of the cell side, perpendicular to deploy_direction_b

SpaceWeatherConfig.atmosphere_table: The profile "tabular" interpolates (ATMOSPHERE_TABLES); written only with "tabular": a scenario without it saves, and hashes, as before.
SpaceWeatherConfig.cache_dir: defaults to engine.spaceweather's own cache dir when None
SpaceWeatherConfig.forecast_percentile: [%] which of MSFC's predicted percentiles drives the days past the observations: 95 conservative (ESA AD10 Sec. 5.9, operations), 50 nominal (AD10, end of life), 5 low
SpaceWeatherConfig.msfc_file_path: your own MSFC prediction table; None = the one shipped with the app

SpacecraftConfig.center_of_mass_b_m: [m] The center of mass from body point B, in body axes (Basilisk's hub.r_BcB_B); inertia_kg_m2 is about this point. Facet locations, thruster and sensor positions stay measured from B, so an offset here gives drag, SRP and thrust their torque about the center of mass.
SpacecraftConfig.control_params: {"K": ..., "P": ...} MRP feedback control gains; see engine.fsw.DEFAULT_MRP_GAINS for the defaults used when a key is absent.
SpacecraftConfig.dry_mass_kg: [kg] The spacecraft's mass WITHOUT station-keeping propellant. With station_keeping unset (the default), this is simply the whole spacecraft's simulated mass, exactly as before StationKeepingConfig existed. With station_keeping set, engine.service initializes the simulated mass to dry_mass_kg + station_keeping.propellant_kg, and the station-keeping controller depletes it back toward dry_mass_kg as propellant burns -- see StationKeepingConfig's docstring.
SpacecraftConfig.enable_drag: Perturbations -- Phase 0's service only ever consumes central-body gravity; these flags are validated/round-tripped now and read starting Phase 1, matching the "reserve the shape, don't wire it all up yet" note.
SpacecraftConfig.enable_gravity_gradient: Torque from the central body's (and, if present, any third-body perturber's) gravity gradient across the spacecraft's own mass distribution -- Basilisk's real GravityGradientEffector, not an approximation: it reads the spacecraft's actual simulated inertia/ position/attitude every tick (see engine.service), so it stays correct through inertia changes (e.g. FuelTank depletion, once that exists) rather than being computed once from initial conditions. Negligible in LEO for an actively-controlled spacecraft (the RW/MRP feedback loop simply rejects it as one more disturbance torque), but real for anything coasting without active control (fsw_mode=None) or in a large/elongated inertia configuration -- exactly the case this schema previously had no way to model at all. False by default: every scenario written before this field existed keeps its exact previous dynamics.
SpacecraftConfig.facets: Optional flat-plate model of the outer surface (list[FacetConfig]). When set, enabled drag and SRP use it (attitude-dependent forces plus their torques) instead of the sphere-like drag_area_m2/drag_coeff and srp_area_m2/srp_coeff above. Needs simulation_mode 'full_attitude'.
SpacecraftConfig.fsw_mode: One of SUPPORTED_FSW_MODES, or None for no attitude control (attitude still integrates -- see engine.service -- it just isn't commanded).
SpacecraftConfig.fsw_params: Mode-specific settings engine.fsw needs to build the guidance chain, e.g. {"sigma_R0N": [...]} for "inertial3D" or {"target_ground_station": "dsn-goldstone", "pHat_B": [0, 0, 1]} for "locationPointing" -- see engine/fsw.py's per-mode builder docstrings for the full set each mode reads.
SpacecraftConfig.landmark_navigation: camera navigation from a small body's landmarks
SpacecraftConfig.model: The spacecraft's 3D model, if one was built or imported in the model editor; see SpacecraftModelConfig.
SpacecraftConfig.model_analyses: The run analyses built on the model and the mounted equipment (ModelAnalysesConfig); None, as every scenario before them: none.
SpacecraftConfig.navigation_error: What simpleNav tells the flight software; None: the true state.
SpacecraftConfig.optical_navigation: camera navigation from the central body's disk

StationKeepingConfig.deadband_km: [km] how far below target_altitude_km before a reboost burn starts
StationKeepingConfig.eccentricity_neutral_burns: Gate firings so a multi-orbit, eclipse-interrupted burn doesn't accumulate an eccentricity change (it waits for the balancing side of the orbit instead).
StationKeepingConfig.eclipse_sunlit_threshold: [-] shadow factor above which the spacecraft is treated as sunlit
StationKeepingConfig.min_on_time_s: [s] minimum firing duration (minimum impulse bit = thrust_n * min_on_time_s)
StationKeepingConfig.propellant_kg: [kg] initial propellant mass available for station-keeping
StationKeepingConfig.target_altitude_km: [km] altitude above the central body's equatorial radius to maintain

ValueMark.reason: why the scenario's value replaces it: required when overridden
ValueMark.value: the value computed or suggested, in the field's own unit
